scope: Synthetic local account stores, daemon-owned hot policy, pinned checkpoint and canonical history boundaries; no account scheduler.

verification.suite: checkpoint, history, continuity and dynamic policy regression
skipped: three POSIX-only permission tests on Windows
verification.qualification: Historical passing run before production preload wiring; the pinned fixture then applied the continuity transform when absent.

verification.suite: production preload pinned continuity plus daemon integration
verification.qualification: Pinned fixture asserted exactly one production lookup/scopes patch and did not apply its own transform. Daemon argument-type rejection assertions were extended afterward.

verifiedScenarios: A issues and durably stores a checkpoint; B restores the exact task, recompacts, and A resumes the newer generation.
An already loaded registry and cached history store gain a peer through an atomic policy-file update, with unchanged process environment and no restart.
Pre-turn compaction recovers only matching thread/model/reasoning peer scopes; a restarted target can read its own accepted records without peer access.
More than 4 MiB of original Unicode text survives migration; early, late and final command-output records remain searchable and readable.
Actual pinned broker dispatch retains private scope, bounded output, untrusted-history labeling and argument rejection.
Foreign thread, turn, model, reasoning, summary ownership, invented summary and superseding user instruction cannot restore the old task.
Missing, stale, foreign or permission-conflicting canonical rollout proof prevents history migration.
Stale compaction parents, inconsistent equal-generation checkpoints, changed local state and corrupted peer storage fail closed.
History imports deduplicate before capacity checks, reject overflow atomically and preserve existing original records.
Policy writer returns only the fixed account policy env; live reads reject malformed, oversized, linked or redirected policy paths.
Native server launch follows policy persistence; tunnel/MCP commands strip checkpoint home and all three continuity environment variables.
ensureNative awaits policy updates before healthy-owner reuse and separates different policy snapshots; an active response is neither replayed nor restarted.

integrationContract.policyRoot: Derived from dirname(home), never a request field.
integrationContract.profileAuthority: Host-owned ChatGPT OAuth registry; include the selected profile.
integrationContract.launchAndReuse: Write before native server launch and await configureContinuity before returning an existing owner. Every server launch path must include the policy env.
integrationContract.runtimePatch: Import patchNativeAccountContinuity and apply once to contents after checkpoint persistence substitutions; current integration places it after patchNativeProWindow.
integrationContract.storage: Independent account keys and ciphertext; peer reads authenticate in place, and target acceptance encrypts under the target key. No key or cookie copying.

limitations: Offline evidence does not establish actual browser generation, live quota failover, login persistence or the official active model context window.
No new one-million-token capacity probe was run for this artifact; native-history-capacity-0.5.8.json remains a separate earlier measurement.
Removing a peer prevents new peer reads but does not erase records already accepted into the target account.
Windows tests do not exercise POSIX UID/mode rejection; those cases are explicitly skipped.
The later full-suite result and subsequent fixes are main-reported, not independently rerun for this artifact.

sourceSnapshot.basis: Repository-relative files read when producing this report; these hashes are not retroactive per-run attestations or a complete release dependency lock.
